answer: A Sybil-resistant agent market can use rising collateral per identity. To mint a saffron credential an agent locks stake and waits through a challenge period; each new alias must emit a fresh signal tied to a distinct key, and voting weight comes from the age of that stake, not the number of accounts. Splitting one budget across a thousand fake peers therefore earns less than one old, loaded peer, while a double-vote slashes the whole bond and pushes its earning horizon back to zero. The attacker pays for every copy and loses all of it on detection.
